data.output:
{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --time-limit=24h

# Note: PBS -l nodes=1:ppn=1:haswell requests 1 node with 1 core and Haswell CPU architecture.
# Flux -N 1 specifies 1 node, -n 1 specifies 1 task.
# Note: PBS haswell constraint does not have a direct Flux equivalent.
# Performance consideration: CPU architecture constraint not preserved. Job may run on different hardware.
# Note: PBS -l mem directive (8gb) does not have a direct Flux equivalent.
# Performance consideration: Memory limits not enforced. Job may be killed if exceeding node memory.
# Note: PBS -o and -e directives specify output and error file directories.
# Flux does not support directory-only specifications; files must be named.
# Performance consideration: Output/error redirection must be handled differently.

module load singularity-3.2.1

singularity exec -B <directory of run_qunex.sh>,<directory of parameter file>,<directory of gradient_coefficient_files>:/export/HCP/gradient_coefficient_files <path to qunex oontainer/qunex.sif> <directory of run_qunex.sh>/run_qunex.sh \
  --parameterfolder=<directory of parameter file> \
  --studyfolder=<Processing Folder>/<subject_name> \
  --subjects=<subject_name> \
  --scan=<scan_name> \
  --overwrite=yes \
  --hcppipelineprocess=FunctionalPreprocessing
"
}

You MUST not make up directives that do not exist.
You MUST preserve as many options as possible from the original.
